note: This file is the sole canonical owner of every token-economy rule, threshold, model route and escalation gate in this repository. The skill, the agent definition and the README section are projections of it and are never read back as a source. Parity is asserted in one direction only, so a drift finding always names the projection that moved.
purpose: Remove token spend that buys nothing, and route what remains to the cheapest model that can carry it safely. Quality is not one of the levers. Every rule below either removes waste or moves work to a cheaper tier at equal safety; none of them removes a check.

qualityFloors.note: A token budget sits a very short distance from 'skip the test' and 'one reviewer is enough'. Each of those trades a real guarantee for a saving that never shows up in a ledger, so they are stated as floors rather than left to judgement.

deterministicChecks.why: an identical live task signature means the answer is already being computed
same path at an unchanged hash; a second read returns bytes already in context
two writers on one change package lose work; the writer may not review itself
a review on a moving tree proves nothing and has to be paid for twice
git refuses it later; discovering that after the work is the expensive path
the resource decision is read, never re-derived from raw numbers
a verdict bound to a superseded snapshot is not evidence about the current one
a failing gate is a fact; asking a model to confirm it costs tokens and changes nothing
a finished panel left open keeps a context alive that nobody is reading

governor.invokedPerWaveRationale: A governor that runs before and after every wave spends tokens on every wave, including the ones two file hashes already settled. The deterministic gate carries those; the model is reached only where no fact can decide.

economics.note: The governor is measured the way it measures everything else. Below the minimum invocation count there is not enough evidence to judge, so it stays on and says so; above it, a net cost switches its automatic invocation off. Switching it off never disables the deterministic gate, which was carrying most of the weight and costs nothing.
economics.thresholdSource: token-economy-policy.json#governor.economics, read by readPolicyEconomics; the CLI never takes thresholds from its caller
economics.ledgerFileIsNotAProjection: token-economy-ledger.json is mutable operational state read back as a source by the economics command. Listing it under projections contradicted this file's own rule that a projection is never read back as a source, so it lives here and only here.
economics.switchIsAdvisory: This repository computes the verdict and exits 5. Acting on it — actually suspending automatic invocation — belongs to the orchestration layer and is not implemented here.

modelRoutingNote: Escalation is driven by task risk and evidence need, never by cost alone and never automatically on failure. A tier is chosen because it is the cheapest one that can carry the decision safely.

doNotUse: any security decision or security review
any architectural or architect-level contract decision

use: test authoring against a stated contract
small fixes with a canonical pattern already in the repository
documentation projection from a canonical source
doNotUse: adversarial review of a security-critical change

fable.ifUnavailable: Do not imitate it and do not invent the name. Report that the identity could not be verified, then choose Sonnet or Opus by task risk.
use: security plus AI-first plus human-input independent review
doNotUse: any run where the model identity has not been verified live

use: a problem a lower tier has failed twice
doNotUse: mechanical inventory a cheaper tier resolves identically

workerPackaging.note: The largest avoidable spend is not the model tier; it is handing a worker a conversation it does not need. A task package carries exactly what the task requires and nothing else.
include: immutable base commit or content hash
exclude: corpus the task does not read

resultReporting.note: A worker returns evidence, not a story. Long output stays where it was produced.

mustNotRunInParallel: writers touching the same file set
phases where one depends on another's output
two owners of the same terminal marker

readerObservability.note: tools/token-guard.mjs reads a real git tree and the guardian admission decision. It cannot see the orchestration-layer registries, so those must be supplied through --facts. Handing back empty arrays for them would report looked-and-found-nothing for checks that were never performed, so the reader returns null and the evaluators escalate.
readerObservability.consequence: A bare CLI run decides four of the nine checks. The five orchestration-layer registries escalate when a request needs them, except completed-panel cleanup, which advises rather than escalating because a leaked panel is a cost report and not a blocking fact. Full nine-check coverage requires --facts from the orchestration layer.
readerObservability.externalDependency: readGuardian shells out to guardianctl, a machine-local binary that is not part of this repository. When it is absent the guardian check escalates rather than passing.

checkerCoverage.note: What check-token-economy.mjs compares, stated so the skill does not imply more.
compared: escalation gates against the guard's exported constant
notCompared: the prose bodies of the skill and agent
checkerCoverage.consequence: Drift inside an uncompared section is invisible to the checker and is caught, if at all, by review.
